verdictRationale: The current spec closes the remaining P1 approval-token contradiction by splitting approval artifacts into signed_token and policy_permit, then binding signature requirements to operator_pubkey presence. Prior severe and showstopper issues remain resolved under regression sweep: heartbeat never applies, autoapply has a separate explicit job, risky approved items become APPROVED_APPLY, telemetry remains default-off, and untrusted manifests cannot apply on non-dev channels.

falsifiability.failureCondition: A P1 install with no operator_pubkey either accepts a signed_token artifact or rejects a matching unsigned policy_permit for a risky rule_change item.
falsifiability.observableSignal: The evaluator output contradicts the artifact-kind signature matrix, causing either signed_token to become APPROVED_APPLY in P1 or policy_permit to become BLOCKED despite exact non-signature bindings.
falsifiability.measurementMethod: Run the AC #17 evaluator matrix in unit tests over signed_token and policy_permit with operator_pubkey set and unset, then run the P1 integration fixture with a rule_change item, one matching unsigned permits[] entry, and one matching token file.
falsifiability.threshold: All four signature-matrix cases match AC #17 exactly, and the P1 integration shows policy_permit APPROVED_APPLY while signed_token is BLOCKED approval_unsigned.

ledgerReview.rationale: Heartbeat and autoapply are now separate jobs, and the P3 path uses autoapply rather than heartbeat-driven apply.
Telemetry remains default OFF and requires both telemetry_enabled true and heartbeat_url before any network adapter is wired.
The risky taxonomy now covers rules, instructions, skills, schemas, and behavior-driving registries, with unknown paths failing strict classification.
Apply is gated on TrustEvidence signed or sha_pinned, with untrusted manifests blocked on non-dev channels.
Rollback now records absence tombstones and uses post-apply SHA checks before deleting update-created files.
Approval artifacts bind manifest_sha, target, category, and expiry, making replay against future manifests explicitly blocked.
The evaluator has an APPROVED_APPLY terminal decision, and the executor plus autoapply gate accept both AUTO_APPLY and APPROVED_APPLY.
P1 no longer requires signed-token success; it uses unsigned policy_permit mode when operator_pubkey is unset and explicitly blocks signed_token artifacts until P3.

preserveList.summary: The spec keeps manifest-pull as the core update model and avoids remote command execution or control-plane push into customer installs.
The PolicyDecision union is closed and executor acceptance is limited to AUTO_APPLY and APPROVED_APPLY, which makes approval behavior testable.
Telemetry is schema-constructed, strict-validated, size-bounded, and default-off, preserving the stated customer privacy posture.
